title: An Endless Supply
text: “I wonder if showing Itsuki some darkness around Siltvelt might change his mind?”

“Nano! Gaelion has a little idea, so Gaelion’s going to take Bow Hero to Shieldfreeden, nano. Gaelion’s governed that place before in a different loop, so Gaelion knows all about darkness there, nano.”

So Rival was planning to take over Shieldfreeden in this loop too! Gnnh… if I let her drag Father into it carelessly, we’d end up with the same outcome as before, indeed. I absolutely had to stop this.
“Really? Well then, maybe I’ll ask Gaelion-chan for help after all.”
“Fufu, I wonder what kind of darkness she’ll show me.”
“Well, even if it doesn’t manage to straighten him out, it might at least let Bow Hero try his hand at being a dark hero, which would probably suit him perfectly, nano.”
“I wonder… would it be some kind of American comic book city?”

Now that I thought about it, from Father’s stories and my own memories of Japan, I felt like I’d seen that kind of overseas superhero movie before. A city of crime, I say. Probably born from the selfish sort of “freedom” Shieldfreeden goes on about. Well, there were quite a lot of reincarnators over there, so a town full of criminals wasn’t entirely out of the question, indeed.
“Ara~ Naofumi-chan and everyone worked so hard. Should Big Sister and I give you all a good pat on the head for it, I wonder~?”
Since Big Sister was around, Older Sister seemed to be joining in on the chatter too, indeed.
“Sadeena-san, I really wish you’d reconsider your phrasing sometimes.”
“Ara? But it’s true that Big Sister wants to thank Naofumi-chan and the others for working so hard, you know?”

“I suppose we did work hard, if you want to call it that… well, whether or not it actually clears up my bad reputation is highly questionable, but at least the circus in Melromarc should be able to restart on better footing now.”
“Yay! We finally get to join the circus in Melromarc!”
Big Sister and the others’ eyes were absolutely sparkling, indeed.

“I think so? The acts that abused demi-humans and beastmen will probably be scrapped given the current mood, and it’ll reopen properly. Might even be nice to have Eclair’s town build a permanent circus facility. That way everyone can enjoy watching it too.”
“Sounds so fun!”
“Let’s ask about it!”
“Yeah!”
“I think that’s a fine idea. I’ll grant my permission as well.”
Father and Older Sister watched on as Big Sister and the others got all excited like that, indeed.
“In between doing what I need to do, I’ll also help Emia and the others rebuild the Lulmo settlement. Though Shieldfreeden does sound interesting too.”

“Well, according to the Queen, soldiers have thinned out quite a bit, so wrongdoers seem to be popping up all over the place… honestly, it’s kind of impressive that villains never run dry even in times like these. There’s a saying in my world: ‘Though the sands of the shore run out, the seeds of thieves in this world shall never cease.’ It fits, word for word.”
“That would be the death poem attributed to Ishikawa Goemon, I believe.”
Actually, there’s a theory that the poem Father recited had been slightly trimmed down, indeed.

“The full version goes, ‘Though the sands of Ishikawa’s shore run out, the seeds of thieves in this world shall never cease.’ Some believe it was meant as an ironic jab—Ishikawa Goemon, captured by officials wary that executing him as a spectacle for theft would turn him into a hero and inspire copycats, is said to have declared, ‘Kill me as a warning all you like, but thieves won’t vanish from this world, will they?’”
“Motoyasu-kun, you really do know a lot about history and stuff, huh.”
“Is that so?”
Father had gone and praised me, indeed. As I’ve mentioned before, I was rather good at school, actually.
“Fufu… quite true, indeed. No matter how much you mow them down, they just keep sprouting up from who knows where. Truly, how lamentable.”
Itsuki’s mocking little laugh really stuck with me during that whole exchange, indeed.

And so, while we were busy relocating the people of Big Sister’s village to the settlement that needed rebuilding and helping out with reconstruction… the captured Crimson Swine was finally hauled off to the castle, so we all gathered to greet it and hand down its punishment. Everyone assembled in the throne room for the welcome, indeed. Well met, Crimson Swine! From here on, you shall be judged and disposed of accordingly, I say. For the record, the Queen was sitting in as proxy on the throne, with Ren—disguised as Rafumi—and Fiancée standing beside her. Filo-tan was standing guard right next to them too, indeed.
“Bu-bu-buhi!? Bu-bu-buhyaaaaaaaaaaaa! Buhyaaaaa!”
The captured swine appeared to be pleading desperately with the Queen and the confined Trash about something, indeed.
“Ugh… it’s saying the exact same thing as that self-centered guy who ran off to become a monk.”
“What kind of comedy sketch is this. It’s honestly kind of funny in its own way.”
Father looked utterly disgusted, while Itsuki let out a little chuckle, indeed.
“Silence!” The Queen glared straight at Trash. “I don’t think you even comprehend how much damage you’ve caused us on this side!”
Trash fell speechless at the swine’s words, indeed.
“Malty…”
Apparently he was stunned into silence because the reddish-black pig had said practically the same thing he himself once had, indeed.
“Furthermore, once you judged that your attempt to win over the Heroes had failed, it seems you sought contact with Takt—an enemy from a world you already knew all too well.”
“Buhi!? Bu-buhi! Bu-bu-bu!”
“A misunderstanding? We have solid testimony confirming you were searching for a criminal named Takt at the time of your capture, you know? Unfortunately, he has already been dealt with.”
“Bu… bu-bu-bu! Bu-buhi.”

“You claim you didn’t know? That you went to Faubrey looking for me? How convenient that sounds. You’ve already acted far too selfishly for me to believe you’d come crying to me for help—and besides, Melty is already here in Melromarc.”
“Buhi!”
“Save your nonsense about being framed for when you’re actually dreaming.”
Father watched this whole exchange between the Queen and the Crimson Swine unfold, indeed. His expression practically screamed serves you right.
“Now then… Aultcray? You go stand with Malty as well.”
Trash trudged over toward the swine as though he’d given up halfway, indeed. But his gaze kept drifting toward Tiger Girl and the others, who had come to the throne room as Father’s allies, indeed.
“Bu, buhi!? Bu-bu-bu-bu!”
The swine had noticed Tiger Girl and was saying something urgently to Trash, indeed.
“Ah… those girls are your relatives, Malty. Even if they’re Hakuko, please don’t let it bother you.”

Trash tried to soothe the swine with a gentle expression, but the swine’s eyes stayed locked on Tiger Girl as though it had just recognized the single greatest threat imaginable. I did not miss that, indeed. Even I had to admit this seemed genuinely dangerous. Which is exactly why I felt it best to bring Tiger Girl in only after the swine had been dealt with, indeed.
“Now then…”

The Queen hid her mouth behind her fan as she turned her gaze toward Father, Itsuki, and myself, indeed. Clearly she wasn’t about to hand out easy mercy. But it also seemed she wanted to find some fitting compromise that took Trash’s feelings into account too.

“All of it—every single opportunity—was nipped in the bud by my incompetent husband and daughter. Simply following Iwatani-sama on your own would have sufficed. Had you drawn him to your side from there and kept him tamed, you’d likely be sitting quite comfortably as the unshakeable heir to the throne by now… though it seems Spear Hero-sama saw through everything from the very start regardless.”
Oh? Here it was—the same condemnation speech for the Crimson Swine as in the very first world, indeed. If I recalled correctly, it went something like this, indeed.
“Bu-bu-buhi!”
“Silence!”
At that, the Queen hurled an ice spell straight into the swine’s face, indeed. Something like a slap, I’d imagine.
“It’s not that he’s unattractive. If anything… Shield Hero-sama has quite a gentle face, doesn’t he.”
Fiancée offered a somewhat gentler rebuttal to the swine’s remark, indeed.
“In any case, you utterly failed at winning over the Heroes and, worse still, sowed discord among us. I intend to see you take responsibility commensurate with that. Next, Aultcray.”
The Queen turned her gaze toward Trash, who offered no resistance and simply let his face turn away, accepting whatever was to come, indeed.
